text:
A: Hiya! Oh, Kasia, is it? I'm Gemma.
B: Hi, Gemma. Yes. I think you're the nurse. Kulwinder said she'd had a nurse.
A: Ha, that's me! She was trying to teach me dal before we got cut off. What do you do?
B: Biomedical scientist. Haematology, in a hospital lab.
A: Oh, no way! So you're the ones who ring us when the potassium's off.
B: Yes, sorry. That's us. Or when the sample is haemolysed and we need another one.
A: Oh, don't. That's every Monday on our ward. The students squeeze the tube.
B: Tell them not to shake it also. People shake it like a cocktail.
A: I will, I'll put it in handover. Where are you based?
B: Warrington. Originally Poland. You?
A: Taunton. Are you on shifts as well, then?
B: Days, mostly, some lates and weekends. I just finished a run of lates, so I'm a bit knackered.
A: Same, three long days. We could just sit here and stare at each other for three minutes.
B: That would be honest research.
A: Ha! Erm, what do you do on your days off?
B: Parkrun sometimes, Victoria Park. Walking with my husband. And the garden, tomatoes.
A: Stop it. Parkrun and tomatoes, that's literally my whole life. Vivary Park, Saturday mornings. What's your time like?
B: Middle. Always middle. Around thirty minutes.
A: Twenty-nine-forty for me, finally, after about a year of being stuck at thirty. I was so chuffed I nearly cried at the finish funnel. Liam, my partner, was like, it's twenty seconds, Gem. And I'm like, it's twenty seconds I've earned!
B: It counts. What does Liam do?
A: He's an electrician.
B: No. My husband is an electrician too. Dan.
A: Shut up! Does he leave his van across the whole road?
B: Across our drive and the neighbour's. And he has the rugby on every evening. Warrington Wolves.
A: Oh, Neil told me about that, the league. Thirteen players, less standing about in heaps, apparently.
B: That's very accurate, actually. Dan would like this Neil.
A: How are your tomatoes this year? Mine finally went red last week, I was so proud.
B: Mine got blight. Kulwinder told me to keep the leaves off the soil. Too late now. Next year.
A: She's like a walking advice column, isn't she? I loved her.
B: She's very direct. I liked that. You know where you are.
A: Exactly. Erm, I saw your photo, you had a clothes airer in the back as well. I felt very seen.
B: There is always an airer. It's the British weather.
A: It's the one thing that never—
B: Oh, it's ending.
